Envelope: every native read and flow read returns one envelope as structured content, with the identical JSON as the text content: data (typed by the reviewed output schema; whole document text is never the default), observed_at, source_revisions, completeness {state, basis, snapshot_consistent}, pagination (null for a single row), freshness and warnings; _meta repeats observed_at and source_revisions. source_revisions always holds the contract and execution digests.

Row revisions: when the read table is enrolled for approved writes (`connector_owner_switches`) and no other connection committed between the data read and the revision read, source_revisions also holds the current row revision of every returned row as `row:<table>/<id>` (when the tool projects id) or the highest returned revision as `rows:<table>`. A revision changes on every insert, update and delete of that row, so a changed value means the row changed. An empty page cites no rows. Revisions cover returned rows only, never the page total or filters, and snapshot_consistent stays false.

No revision: otherwise (not enrolled, enrollment triggers altered, a write interleaved, a point-in-time as_of read, a single-connection pool, more concurrent reads than half the database pool, or a flow read) the warning data_revision_unavailable stays and no row revision is cited.

Writes use other shapes: a write result is not this envelope. A command tool returns the operation envelope {operation_id, preview, expires_at, review_url}, and _commit and _status return the receipt/status view, each also mirrored as identical JSON text.
